description:
The city of Montreal suffered a series of failures (1932, 1944, 1956) in its bids to host the
Winter Games under the leadership of Camillien Houde, before finally hosting the 1976
Olympic Games. These attempts helped to build a local Olympic culture and accumulate
valuable expertise. The arrival of Jean Drapeau as mayor marked a turning point, as he was
inspired by the Olympic ideal and led an intensive diplomatic campaign, using Expo 67 to
win over the International Olympic Committee (IOC). Despite the failure to host the 1972
Summer Games, his strategy, combining geopolitical alliances, promotion of Olympism, and
promotion of Montreal’s multicultural identity, ultimately paid off: on May 12, 1970, the city
was designated to host the 1976 Games. These Games, held from July 17 to August 1, 1976,
crowned a century of ambition and permanently transformed the city, making the Olympic
Games a catalyst for modernization and international recognition. Montreal thus embodies the

name: From Camillien Houde to Jean Drapeau: a history of Montreal's Olympic bids

description: Intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) data offer a unique combination of high spatial and temporal resolution measures of the living human brain. However, data collection is limited to highly specialized clinical environments. To improve internal (re)use and external sharing of these unique data, we present a structure for storing and sharing iEEG data: BIDS-iEEG, an extension of the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) specification, along with freely available examples and a bids-starter-kit. BIDS is a framework for organizing and documenting data and metadata with the aim to make datasets more transparent and reusable and to improve reproducibility of research. It is a community-driven specification with an inclusive decision-making process. As an extension of the BIDS specification, BIDS-iEEG facilitates integration with other modalities such as fMRI, MEG, and EEG. name: BIDS-iEEG: an extension to the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) Specification for intracranial electroencephalography

description:
This EEG data set was recorded by the PainLabMunich (https://painlabmunich.de/) at the Technical University of Munich (TUM). 166 healthy participants took part in two identical experimental sessions, which were separated by one month. In each session, participants underwent a five-minute-long eyes-closed resting state recording. This was followed by an experimental pain paradigm applying 80 brief painful laser stimuli at 4 different intensities, for each of which a verbal pain rating was collected. Brain activity was recorded using EEG and skin conductance responses were measured. Prior to EEG recordings and EEG cap preparation, demographic and psychological variables were collected in each session, including questionnaires about sleep quality, anxiety and depression, positive and negative affect, and pain sensitivity. The original preregistration of the study can be found here: https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT05616091.
